forecasts.label: Capital financing requirement
forecasts.note: Restated at each quarterly return. The Q4 restatement comes from the annual return itself, so it lands on the outturn by construction — the interesting movement is Q1 to Q3.

forecasts.label: Interest payable
forecasts.note: The council's own full-year forecast, restated at each quarterly return.

forecasts.label: Revenue spending (net current expenditure)
forecasts.note: The full-year forecast of net current expenditure — the running cost of services — restated each quarter against the same measure at outturn.

forecasts.label: Capital expenditure
forecasts.note: Total capital spending forecast each quarter (the capital payments return) against the annual capital outturn. Capital spending not met from grants or receipts is what turns into new borrowing, so a forecast running ahead of outturn is a borrowing signal.

in_year.label: Interest payable, as reported each quarter
in_year.note: Per quarter, not cumulative. The quarterly return is a lighter collection than the annual one and sums to roughly 92% of it nationally, so the two are shown apart rather than added together.

news_drafts.headline: North Hertfordshire delays £3m of asset sales to secure better value, increasing internal borrowing
news_drafts.lead:
North Hertfordshire District Council expects £3m of income from asset sales to arrive later than planned, because it wants to secure better value when it disposes of the assets. The first-quarter capital budget monitoring report, taken by Cabinet on 22 September 2026, sets out the change.

The money had been forecast as capital receipts, the proceeds of selling assets, which councils can use to pay for capital spending, meaning money spent on things that last, such as buildings and equipment. Until the sales go through, the council will fill the gap by using its own cash instead of taking a loan, known as internal borrowing, which saves interest but uses up the council's cash cushion.

The paper also says the delay will raise the council's minimum revenue provision in future years. That is the amount a council must set aside from each year's budget to pay off past borrowing, much like a mortgage repayment. The report says: "The delay would mean an increase in internal borrowing and the minimum revenue provision in future years until those capital receipts were realised and could be applied as capital funding." The higher charge therefore adds to day-to-day running costs until the sales are completed and the receipts can be applied.

findings.headline: Planned service desk development efficiency no longer achievable as work shifts from in-house development to external procurement.
findings.detail: Planned ongoing efficiency saving of £25k from in-house development of new service desk solution will not be achieved. Originally intended as internal development project to deliver efficiency, but due to its complexity and technical resources being absorbed by LGR support requirements, system must now be procured externally. External procurement deferred to next financial year with £25k carry forward requested. Ongoing annual support and maintenance costs also expected to be significantly higher than estimated as market has moved away from locally hosted software to subscription-based cloud platforms (£44k estimated 2027/28 impact).
findings.matters: Planned efficiency not being delivered due to resource constraints and technical complexity; external procurement costs higher than originally assumed.
findings.figures: £25k planned efficiency not achieved, £25k carry forward, £44k estimated 2027/28 impact
findings.quote: The planned ongoing saving from the service desk being developed in house will not be achieved, as explained in table three above. £25k underachievement.

findings.headline: Thomas Bellamy House future use uncertain; lettings income delayed indefinitely to Autumn 2027 at earliest.
findings.detail: Future use of Thomas Bellamy House property remains uncertain. Options appraisal expected to be completed in current year to consider potential letting arrangements, capital expenditure requirements, and potential capital receipt from sale. No income anticipated prior to Autumn 2027 at earliest pending completion of appraisal and subsequent decisions. Creates £37k current year budget shortfall and estimated £19k impact on 2027/28.
findings.matters: Budgeted property letting income deferred indefinitely; property disposition strategy unclear creating multi-year revenue uncertainty.
findings.quote: The future use of Thomas Bellamy House remains uncertain... Income from letting would not be anticipated prior to Autumn 2027 at the earliest, pending the outcome of the appraisal and subsequent decisions.

findings.headline: Solar for Business Initiative project closed without completing any installations, losing £21k planned efficiency.
findings.detail: Solar for Business Initiative was intended to generate income and deliver £21k efficiency saving but project has closed without any installations being completed due to difficulties attracting suitable business interest. Scheme has generated no income and efficiency has not been achieved, creating £21k contribution to overall efficiency shortfall of £59k in quarter one.
findings.matters: Planned efficiency not being delivered; market did not develop as anticipated for this income/savings opportunity.
findings.quote: This project was closed without any installations being completed, due to difficulties in attracting suitable business interest. As a result, the scheme has not generated any income.

findings.headline: Multiple capital and digital projects deferred or paused, primarily citing Local Government Reorganisation uncertainty.
findings.detail: Careline call handling system procurement deferred to March 2027 completion (implementation costs now expected in 2027/28). Careline service desk solution carry forward requested for 2027/28 due to complexity and technical resources absorbed by LGR support requirements. Agile AI procurement paused following Hertfordshire County Council decision not to lead and other councils' collaboration not progressing due to LGR. Idox Insights installation deferred pending LGR decisions. Royston Town Council Annexe redevelopment delayed awaiting access resolution and car park renewal with HCC. Total of approximately £94k requested carry forwards plus other deferred strategic investments.
findings.matters: Multiple strategic project deferrals indicate substantial LGR uncertainty affecting investment and service delivery planning across multiple directorates.
findings.figures: £25k Careline service desk carry forward, £34k Careline call handling carry forward, £45k planning software carry forward, £20k Royston annexe carry forward
findings.quote: Progress with the procurement of Agile AI has however been paused in the new financial year following the Hertfordshire County Council decision not to lead on the procurement and the subsequent collaboration with other Councils not progressing due to LGR.

findings.headline: Business rates collection forecast below government's baseline assessment but protected by one-year only 100% safety net.
findings.detail: Reset of business rates retention system on 1 April 2026 updated council's baseline. Council currently expects to collect less business rates income than the Baseline Rates by Baseline, which would normally leave it below baseline funding level. However, government has set safety net at 100% of baseline funding level for 2026/27 only (normally 92.5%), providing £432k top-up funding. This protection expires after 2026/27, creating funding vulnerability for 2027/28 and beyond.
findings.matters: Business rates funding below government's assessed need for the council; temporary protection expires next year, creating funding risk.
findings.figures: 100% safety net (normally 92.5%), £432k safety net funding for 2026/27 only
findings.quote: for 2026/27 only the government has set the safety net at 100%. Based on the forecast business rates position declared to Government in January, the Council will receive £432k of safety net funding in 2026/27.
